[2026-11-24] r:6045053970 review COMMENTED by janb84 (member):
Concept ACK

After going back and forward on this PR, I have to agree with @maflcko and prefer the by-value std::vector constructor as the public interface.

If i'm correct the braced lists are the common case in the tests which this constructor is meant to clean up.  A range template can't take those, so every such call site would still need a `std::array` wrapper.

On the txpackage_tests example: as written it doesn't compile against this PR. CTxIn(COutPoint) is explicit, so a range of COutPoint doesn't satisfy RangeOf<CTxIn>, and package has to stay a real Package because the test shuffles it and appends the child.

So if i fix the example, the two versions are:

```cpp
// range constructor
const CTransaction child{
    package | std::views::transform([](const CTransactionRef& parent) { return CTxIn{COutPoint{parent->GetHash(), 0}}; }),
    std::array{CTxOut{47 * COIN, spk2}}, // a braced list doesn't compile next to a view
};

// vector constructor
std::vector<CTxIn> inputs;
for (const auto& parent : package) inputs.emplace_back(COutPoint{parent->GetHash(), 0});
const CTransaction child{std::move(inputs), {CTxOut{47 * COIN, spk2}}};
```

So the range version saves one line in C++20, and nothing once `std::ranges::to` is available. And in the corrected version the readability diff is weak imho.

My strong preference currently (if I have not missed a angle)  is to land the by-value vector constructor here and add the range overload as a follow-up once there's a real view-shaped caller that needs it.
